words: play; try; idea; together; problem; sketchbook
notes: Play with paint, clay, paper and found things to find ideas, then work with a partner on a small art problem such as a bridge for a toy. Pages go into a first sketchbook. What changes: the first sketchbook is started by play and a partner, with no earlier art work behind it. Assessed by a sketchbook check: the teacher marks each child's idea pages as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: the first sketchbook is a folder of loose sheets.

words: explore; look closely; research; idea; classmates; sketchbook
notes: Explore materials with classmates, then look closely at a real object or picture and research it by drawing before making a work of art. What changes: looking and drawing a real object now come before making, where kindergarten started from play alone. Assessed by a sketchbook check: the teacher marks each child's idea pages as met, partly or not yet.

words: many ways; partner; question; solve; materials; interest
notes: Come up with many ways, with a partner, to solve one art problem, and follow a personal question into a made work using different materials. What changes: many solutions and a question of the child's own. Assessed by a sketchbook check: the teacher marks each child's idea pages as met, partly or not yet.

words: imagine; detail; depth; tool; resource; technology
notes: Add detail and depth to a made-up idea, and use the resources, tools and technology on hand to pursue it, such as a free drawing program or paper and a mirror. What changes: ideas get detail and children choose tools. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the idea pages and a short note on how the best idea grew, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: brainstorm; goal; group; design problem; maker; plan
notes: Brainstorm several ways to tackle a design problem, then set goals as a group for an artwork that matters to its makers. What changes: the group sets a shared goal and each child brings several routes to it, where grade 3 grew one idea alone. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the idea pages and a short note on how the best idea grew, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: merge; fresh idea; research; method; interview; choose
notes: Merge two ideas into a fresh one, and show and name more than one way of researching art (looking, interviewing, sketching, reading) before choosing one to start. What changes: two ideas are merged, and the child names and picks a research method before starting, where grade 4 only listed routes. Assessed by a portfolio entry: the idea pages and a short note on how the best idea grew, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: inquiry; question; source; concept; collaborate; plan
notes: Join ideas with classmates to produce fresh ones, and plan an inquiry into content that matters to the student, with a question, sources and a first sketch. What changes: a planned inquiry rather than a single prompt. Assessed by a planning page and a short talk, scored on a rubric for range of ideas and use of research.

words: stuck; strategy; guideline; aim; limit; restart
notes: Use strategies to get past being stuck (change the material, set a limit, start from a different edge), and write guidelines to steer a work toward a stated aim. What changes: strategies for being stuck and written guidelines. Assessed by a planning page and a short talk, scored on a rubric for range of ideas and use of research.

words: record; process; inquiry; contemporary; daily life; medium
notes: Keep a record of early creative steps as pictures or words in an old or new medium, and with a group shape a question about modern daily life that draws on current art or design. What changes: the record of early steps is kept as it happens, and the group inquiry looks at the present day, not a past style. Assessed by a planning page and a short talk, scored on a rubric for range of ideas and use of research.

words: route; start; inquiry; contemporary; practice; design
notes: Try several routes to start a creative project, and shape an inquiry into modern daily life through current art or design practice. What changes: the student tries several start routes and frames a question about daily life through current practice, with no teacher-set prompt as in grade 8. Assessed by a planning portfolio entry scored on a rubric for range, research and a stated aim. Level 1 bridge: the first unit teaches the grade 8 techniques and words Level 1 needs, as readiness, and claims no grade 8 id (6 days on the 80-day short path, STANDARD.md 3.2).

words: pose; problem; earlier work; select; method; plan
notes: Pose fresh creative problems drawn from the student's own earlier artwork, alone or with others, and choose among materials and methods, old and new, to plan pieces. What changes: problems come from the student's own earlier work. Assessed by a planning portfolio entry scored on a rubric for range, research and a stated aim. Level 2 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: predict; social change; series; theme; norm; material
notes: Plan art or design that could move a community toward a change, and plan a themed series that follows or breaks a norm on purpose, using old and new materials. What changes: the plan carries a social aim and runs as a series, where level 2 planned single pieces from the student's own earlier work. Assessed by a planning portfolio entry scored on a rubric for range, research and a stated aim. Level 3 opens with a review unit of at most 6 days that serves as placement.

words: experiment; paint; clay; safe; non-toxic; tool
notes: Experiment with paint, clay, crayon and paper to build skill, and pick safe, non-toxic supplies and tools with the teacher. What changes: the first hands on tools: experiment with media and pick safe supplies with the teacher. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher watches each child handle one tool safely and marks it as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: only supplies labelled non-toxic; no small items in the mouth; scissors and glue shown before use.

words: try; tool; material; safe; handle; clean up
notes: Try what materials and tools can do, and show the safe grip and handling for each tool before using it for real work. What changes: the child shows safe handling aloud and in action before using a tool, where kindergarten picked supplies with the teacher. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher watches each child handle one tool safely and marks it as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: show and practise each tool's safe grip before the first use.

words: choose; interest; clean; studio; tool; gear
notes: Try varied materials and tools to follow a personal interest, and show safe ways to use and clean tools, gear and the studio area. What changes: a personal choice of material and cleaning as part of the job. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher watches each child handle one tool safely and marks it as met, partly or not yet.

words: process; printing; collage; modeling; finish; skilled
notes: Make a finished artwork the child is happy with, using more than one process and material, and show safe, skilled handling across the processes (for example printing, collage and modeling). What changes: one finished work now crosses several processes, where grade 2 tried materials one at a time. Assessed by a studio task scored on a short rubric for safe handling, care of materials and trying a new technique.

words: technique; invent; care; equipment; safe; hurt
notes: Try out and invent personal art-making techniques, and handle supplies, tools and equipment with care so no one is hurt. What changes: inventing techniques and a duty of care to others. Assessed by a studio task scored on a short rubric for safe handling, care of materials and trying a new technique. Teacher note: sharp tools only after a safe-handling check.

words: practice; skill; craft; care; log; technique
notes: Build skill in several techniques through experiments and practice logged in the sketchbook, and show fine craft by caring for and using supplies and tools well. What changes: practice is logged and craft means care. Assessed by a studio task scored on a short rubric for safe handling, care of materials and trying a new technique.

words: open; new method; environment; waste; reuse; cleanup
notes: Show openness to new ideas, materials and methods, and explain how saving, caring for and cleaning up supplies affects the environment (waste, rinse water, reuse). What changes: the student explains the environmental cost of waste and rinse water, where grade 5 judged craft by care alone. Assessed by a studio task and a practice log, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and persistence.

words: persist; skill; online; permission; share; duty
notes: Keep at it while building skill with varied materials and methods, and show awareness of duty to self and others when sharing images online (permission, names, faces). What changes: persistence is shown over weeks and sharing carries duty. Assessed by a studio task and a practice log, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and persistence.

words: risk; invent; copyright; fair use; open licence; borrow
notes: Show willingness to try, invent and risk ideas in pursuit of meaning, and explain how copyright, fair use, borrowing and open licences apply to the student's own artwork. What changes: the student takes a risk with an idea and explains how copyright and open licences apply to own work, where grade 7 attended to sharing images. Assessed by a studio task and a practice log, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and persistence. Teacher note: only public domain or openly licensed sources are used as models in the unit.

words: unplanned; material; hazard; health; ventilation; safety
notes: Make an artwork or design without planning it first, to learn what the materials do, and explain how materials can affect people's health and nature while handling them safely. What changes: the student makes without planning first to learn what a material does, and explains its health and nature effects, with the hazard sheet read before use. Assessed by a studio task and a portfolio entry, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and sound reasons. Teacher note: a hazard sheet for each material is read before use; ventilation and cleanup are shown.

words: persistence; skill; ethics; consent; credit; documentation
notes: Show gained skill and knowledge in the student's art form through experiments and persistence documented over a term, and show understanding of the ethics of making and sharing creative work (credit, consent, cultural care). What changes: skill growth is documented over a term, and the ethics of making and sharing (credit, consent, cultural care) are reasoned, not just followed. Assessed by a studio task and a portfolio entry, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and sound reasons.

words: theme; series; liberty; duty; image; ethics
notes: Try ideas, plan and make several works on a theme that matters to the student, and weigh liberty against duty when using and sharing images, materials and tools. What changes: a theme across several works and a reasoned view on freedom and duty. Assessed by a studio task and a portfolio entry, scored on a rubric for safe handling, skill growth and sound reasons.

words: place; tree; building; story; my life; draw
notes: Make art that shows the natural and built places around the child, such as a tree, a school or a street, and tell a story from the child's own life in a picture. What changes: first art that shows places and a story from the child's own life. Assessed by a product check: the finished piece and a short talk, marked on a three-line guide. Teacher note: invite stories, never require a private one.

words: sort; object; use; diagram; sculpture; reasons
notes: Sort everyday objects by what they are used for in drawings, diagrams or sculpture, and name when, where and why people make art beyond school. What changes: objects are sorted by use, and art is placed beyond school. Assessed by a product check: the finished piece and a short talk, marked on a three-line guide.

words: reuse; transform; object; event; community; new use
notes: Give an old object a new use by turning it into something else, and make art about events at home, at school or in the community. What changes: reuse and a community event as subject. Assessed by a product check: the finished piece and a short talk, marked on a three-line guide.

words: model; map; diagram; place; observe; scale
notes: Alone or together, make a model, diagram or map of a familiar place, and make an artwork drawn from what the child sees around them. What changes: models and maps of a real place. Assessed by a made product scored on a short rubric for a clear purpose, use of the given need and care in making.

words: region; record; depict; building; place; look closely
notes: Record and depict built places in the region by looking at them, and describe what you recorded. What changes: places are recorded from observation of the real thing, where grade 3 mapped places from memory. Assessed by a made product scored on a short rubric for a clear purpose, use of the given need and care in making.

words: place; object; matters; record; vocabulary; symmetry
cross_subject: math:4.G.A.3 (finding lines of symmetry in a design)
notes: Name, describe and record in pictures the places or objects that matter to the student, and use art and design words to see the student's world freshly. What changes: choosing what matters and using the vocabulary. Assessed by a made product scored on a short rubric for a clear purpose, use of the given need and care in making.

words: user; need; rework; system; design; interest
notes: Create or rework an object, place or system for the stated needs of named users, and note what each user needs. What changes: a design is made for named users and their stated needs, not for the maker's taste. Assessed by a made product and a design note, scored on a rubric for meeting the stated need and clear organizing.

words: hierarchy; layout; contrast; scale; information; gather
cross_subject: math:7.G.A.1 (a scale drawing of a layout)
notes: Apply visual organizing strategies (hierarchy, grouping, scale, contrast) to make work that clearly shares information, and document where and when people gather for art in the community. What changes: a design job is now organizing information so a viewer reads it clearly, where grade 6 met the needs of users. Assessed by a made product and a design note, scored on a rubric for meeting the stated need and clear organizing.

words: layout; text; image; presentation; group identity; audience
notes: Pick and arrange pictures and text so a presentation is clear and compelling to an audience, and make art with a group that reflects on its identity. What changes: pictures and text are arranged together for an audience, where grade 7 organized information alone. Assessed by a made product and a design note, scored on a rubric for meeting the stated need and clear organizing.

words: propose; space; experience; develop; spark; model
notes: With others, propose a work or space that changes how people experience one place, and record how ideas grow from first spark to fully developed idea. What changes: the student proposes a change to one place with others, drawn and modeled, and records how an idea grew, where grade 8 made art together without a site. Assessed by a made product and a written rationale, scored on a rubric for the stated need, the audience and the use of art vocabulary. Teacher note: proposals are drawings and models; nothing is built on school grounds without permission.

words: rework; issue; research; investigate; experiment; system
notes: Rework a thing, a system or a place in response to a current issue, and observe, research and experiment to investigate an unfamiliar topic while making. What changes: an issue drives the redesign and research is documented. Assessed by a made product and a written rationale, scored on a rubric for the stated need, the audience and the use of art vocabulary.

words: culture; image; object; society; history; argument
notes: Make art that shows how a culture's images and objects help or hinder people's lives, joining art-making with knowledge of society, history and personal life. What changes: art is used to argue a view and back it with named sources, where level 2 reworked things in answer to an issue. Assessed by a made product and a written rationale, scored on a rubric for the stated need, the audience and the use of art vocabulary. Teacher note: sources are named and sensitive subjects get a reading by a second adult before the work is shown.

words: tell; make; choose; color; shape; mix
notes: Tell how the child makes art as the child works, using pictures and a few words ('I mixed blue and yellow'). What changes: the first telling: the child says aloud how they make art as they work. Assessed by a talk: each child names one choice and one change, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: describe the making, never grade the picture.

words: line; shape; color; texture; choice; art word
notes: Use art words to tell the choices made while making art (color, line, shape, texture). What changes: the child uses art words for choices, where kindergarten used everyday words. Assessed by a talk: each child names one choice and one change, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: classmate; ask; answer; choice; talk; turn
notes: Talk with classmates about the choices made while making an artwork, taking turns to ask a question and answer it. What changes: the child holds a two-way talk with a classmate about choices, where grade 1 named choices alone. Assessed by a talk: each child names one choice and one change, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: detail; meaning; strengthen; partner; add; change
cross_subject: ela:SL.3.1 (taking part in a collaborative talk with a partner)
notes: Add detail to an artwork to strengthen the meaning that is appearing, after a short talk with a partner. What changes: the child changes the work to strengthen its meaning. Assessed by a critique and a revised piece, scored on a short rubric for using classmate talk and art words.

words: critique; feedback; revise; step; group; change
notes: Change an artwork in progress using ideas from classmate talk in a small-group critique with set steps. What changes: a protocol with steps and a revision made from the talk. Assessed by a critique and a revised piece, scored on a short rubric for using classmate talk and art words.

words: artist statement; explain; choice; revise; art words; critique
notes: Write an artist statement that uses art words to explain choices, then revise the work and the statement after a critique. What changes: the child writes an artist statement, where grade 4 spoke in a critique. Assessed by a critique and a revised piece, scored on a short rubric for using classmate talk and art words.

words: intent; viewer; match; revise; critique; message
notes: Check whether an artwork gets across what was meant, using a critique and a viewer's retelling, and change it to match. What changes: intent is compared with what viewers see. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and a written statement, scored on a rubric for evidence and a reasoned change.

words: reflect; key point; statement; format; explain; evidence
notes: Reflect on a work and explain its key points in a statement or another way (a recorded talk or a labelled sketch). What changes: the child picks the format of the reflection (a statement, a recorded talk or a labelled sketch). Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and a written statement, scored on a rubric for evidence and a reasoned change.

words: standard; examine; unfinished; plan; revise; criteria
notes: Use fitting standards to examine and think over unfinished art, then plan changes in writing before making them. What changes: named standards guide the examination of unfinished work and changes are planned in writing before they are made. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and a written statement, scored on a rubric for evidence and a reasoned change. Teacher note: critique is of the work, never of the person.

words: standard; culture; review; revise; unfinished; past
notes: Use standards from past and present cultures to review and revise unfinished art, naming whose standards are used. What changes: the review uses standards from more than one culture and names whose they are. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and an artist statement, scored on a rubric for standards used, reasons given and the quality of the revision.

words: critique; reflect; rework; polish; vision; draft
notes: After a classmate critique, reflect, rework and polish a work toward the student's own vision, keeping the draft and final side by side. What changes: the student's vision, not only the standards, sets the aim. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and an artist statement, scored on a rubric for standards used, reasons given and the quality of the revision.

words: revisit; polish; standard; vision; defend; statement
notes: Revisit and polish art or design with old and new standards and the student's vision, and defend the changes in a short statement. What changes: every change made after the review is defended with a reason, where level 2 polished toward the student's vision. Assessed by a critique, a revised piece and an artist statement, scored on a rubric for standards used, reasons given and the quality of the revision.

words: choose; collection; keep; display; favorite; why
notes: Choose a few art objects for a small collection of your own and say why, and tell why people keep a collection or a portfolio of work. What changes: first choosing of objects to keep and show. Assessed by a product check: the child shows a chosen piece and says why, marked on a three-line guide. Teacher note: the child's collection is of the child's own choosing; the teacher keeps a folder of the child's work.

words: prize; ready; show; where; when; how
notes: Explain why people prize certain objects and artworks, and ask and answer when, where and how to get a work ready to show. What changes: the child asks and answers when, where and how to prepare a work for showing, where kindergarten only chose. Assessed by a product check: the child shows a chosen piece and says why, marked on a three-line guide.

words: theme; group; exhibit; mount; label; display
notes: Group artworks around a shared theme for an exhibit, and tell apart the materials or ways used to get work ready for display (mounting, labels, frames). What changes: works are grouped by theme and the display materials (mounting, labels, frames) are told apart. Assessed by a product check: the child shows a chosen piece and says why, marked on a three-line guide.

words: space; online; gallery; artist note; choose; ready
notes: Discuss what spaces, including online ones, can and cannot do for showing art, and choose a space and ready the work with artist notes. What changes: a chosen space and a written artist note. Assessed by a display task and a short written note, scored on a rubric for a clear plan and a reason for each choice.

words: technology; keep; guard; format; preserve; change
notes: Explain how technology, old and new, has changed the keeping and showing of art, and what matters when showing and guarding art in different places and formats. What changes: technology across time is weighed, where grade 3 chose a space and wrote a note. Assessed by a display task and a short written note, scored on a rubric for a clear plan and a reason for each choice.

words: curator; care; role; safe; prepare; argue
notes: Define a curator's role and the skills needed to care for and show art, and argue for safe, effective materials and ways of preparing a work for showing. What changes: a named role and an argument with reasons. Assessed by a display task and a short written note, scored on a rubric for a clear plan and a reason for each choice.

words: flat; 3D; digital; display plan; viewer; layout
notes: Compare how flat, three-dimensional and digital art are kept and shown, and draw a display plan, alone or in a group, that fits space, viewers and layout. What changes: a drawn display plan replaces a talk about spaces. Assessed by a display plan and a spoken talk, scored on a rubric for audience, space and reasons.

words: compare; technology; standard; judge; method; viewing
notes: Compare how technology has changed the way art is kept, shown and seen, and judge methods for getting work ready and showing it against set standards. What changes: methods of preparing and showing are judged against standards, where grade 6 drew a plan. Assessed by a display plan and a spoken talk, scored on a rubric for audience, space and reasons.

words: standard; group show; theme; exhibition story; viewer; select
notes: Make standards to judge a group of artworks for a show, then with a group ready and show themed work and write exhibition stories for viewers. What changes: a group show goes up with written stories for its viewers, not a plan alone. Assessed by a display plan and a spoken talk, scored on a rubric for audience, space and reasons. Teacher note: a showing outside class needs each family's yes.

words: curate; analyze; exhibition; keep; choose; judge
notes: Choose and curate works to show and keep, and judge why an exhibition is shown the way it is. What changes: the student acts as curator and critic of a whole show, where grade 8 only planned one with a group. Assessed by an exhibition plan with written reasons, scored on a rubric for audience, space, care of the work and sound reasons.

words: portfolio; select; critique; site; method; show
notes: Analyze, choose and critique the student's own art for a portfolio or collection show, and select methods that suit showing work in one particular place. What changes: the student's own portfolio and a site-specific plan. Assessed by an exhibition plan with written reasons, scored on a rubric for audience, space, care of the work and sound reasons.

words: curate; present; justify; event; conservation; protect
notes: Curate and present art for an exhibit or event with a reason for each choice, and compare ways of keeping and protecting art. What changes: choices are justified for a public event and conservation is researched, where level 2 sited the student's own portfolio. Assessed by an exhibition plan with written reasons, scored on a rubric for audience, space, care of the work and sound reasons.

words: museum; art; building; visit; look; for
notes: Tell what a museum of art is and how it differs from an ordinary building, and tell what one artwork is for. What changes: the first idea of a museum and of an artwork's use. Assessed by a talk: the child tells one use of art, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: a class visit, or a virtual visit with a museum's own free pages.

words: museum; job; visitor; reason; long ago; place
notes: Name what people do who work at or visit museums and art venues, and give reasons people in different places and times made art. What changes: museum jobs are named, and several reasons for making art replace one. Assessed by a talk: the child tells one use of art, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: community; public art; culture; era; compare; use
notes: Explain how art shown in a museum or a public square helps a community, and compare how two cultures used art in different times and places. What changes: two cultures' uses of art are set side by side, where grade 1 listed reasons. Assessed by a talk: the child tells one use of art, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: story; history; record; setting; time; place
notes: Describe the ways and places cultures use art to tell stories and record history, and recognize that reactions to a work change with knowledge of its time and place. What changes: art as story and record, and setting changes a reaction. Assessed by a short written or spoken response citing one work and its setting, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: gallery; aim; experience; infer; clue; culture; tradition; community
notes: Compare what museums, galleries and similar venues aim to offer, look closely to infer when, where and in what culture a work was made, and make art that shows a community's traditions drawn from a community source. What changes: setting is inferred from clues, and a community tradition is shown only from a source the community offers. Assessed by a short written or spoken response citing one work and its setting, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: evidence; show; topic; belief; value; change
notes: Show from a real exhibit or its pages how it carries an idea or information on a topic, and describe how art can change what people believe, value or do. What changes: the student points to evidence in a real exhibit, not just describes what museums do. Assessed by a short written or spoken response citing one work and its setting, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: community; history; value; mirror; custom; era
cross_subject: social-studies:ss6-paleolithic-neolithic (cave art studied with its time and place)
notes: Judge, with evidence, how a museum reflects a community's history and values, and analyze how art mirrors changing eras, customs, supplies and uses. What changes: a museum is judged with evidence, where grade 5 pointed to evidence in one exhibit. Assessed by a source-based response that uses a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence and a stated tie. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: venue; collection; setting; supplies; reaction; compare
notes: Compare what it is like to view collections and exhibits in different venues, and analyze how knowing a work's era, place, supplies and uses shapes the way people react to it. What changes: the student compares what it is like to see an exhibit in different venues, and how knowing a work's era, place and use changes a reaction. Assessed by a source-based response that uses a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence and a stated tie. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: influence; belief; collection; group identity; represent; mirror
notes: Examine how an exhibition or a collection can shape thoughts, beliefs and experience, and tell apart the ways art stands for, builds, strengthens and mirrors a group's identity. What changes: art is tied to group identity, where grade 7 compared venues. Assessed by a source-based response that uses a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence and a stated tie. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: exhibit; society; politics; culture; custom; reaction
notes: Analyze how an exhibit shapes awareness of society, culture and politics, and describe how knowing a culture, its customs and history can change a viewer's reaction to a work. What changes: politics and society now enter the analysis of an exhibit, where grade 8 looked at group identity. Assessed by a source-based response with a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence, setting and a reasoned claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: history; link; defend; society; local; compare
notes: Argue for links between art and the history of society, culture and politics, and compare uses of art across societies and eras with modern local uses. What changes: links are argued and defended, where level 1 only analyzed how an exhibit shaped awareness. Assessed by a source-based response with a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence, setting and a reasoned claim. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: curate; collection; influence; belief; society; experience
notes: Curate a collection that helps viewers grasp a social, cultural or political experience, and judge how an artist or group changed a society's beliefs, values and actions. What changes: the student builds the collection and judges influence on a society, where level 2 defended links. Assessed by a source-based response with a work card for each work, scored on a rubric for evidence, setting and a reasoned claim. Teacher note: a collection on a sensitive subject is read by a second adult before it is shown. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: picture; show; look; see; art; around us
notes: Name the ways art appears in the child's surroundings and tell what a picture shows, using look and tell routines on photos and paintings. What changes: first looking: name where art appears nearby and say what a picture shows. Assessed by a talk: the child says what they see and one feeling, marked as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: use images with plain subjects first.

words: everyday; compare; same; different; subject; describe
notes: Pick and describe artworks that show everyday life, and compare two pictures of the same subject. What changes: two pictures of one subject are compared, where kindergarten described one. Assessed by a talk: the child says what they see and one feeling, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: feeling; sort; mood; nature; building; describe
notes: Notice and describe the look and feel of natural and built surroundings, and sort pictures by the feelings they express. What changes: feelings become a way to sort pictures, where grade 1 compared by subject. Assessed by a talk: the child says what they see and one feeling, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: guess; clue; process; message; picture; because
notes: Guess how an artist went about making an artwork from clues, and work out the messages a picture sends. What changes: guessing process and message from evidence in the picture. Assessed by a short spoken or written response using look-describe-interpret, scored on a three-line guide.

words: before; after; part; message; image; reaction
notes: Compare the child's reactions to an artwork before and after making something similar, and analyze the parts of an image that deliver its message. What changes: parts of the image are named as carriers of a message. Assessed by a short spoken or written response using look-describe-interpret, scored on a three-line guide.

words: reading; others; culture; link; image; compare
notes: Compare your own reading of an artwork with how others read it, and find and analyze cultural links a picture suggests. What changes: other readings are weighed, and culture becomes a clue in the picture. Assessed by a short spoken or written response using look-describe-interpret, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: interpret; persuade; culture; visual part; feeling; action
notes: Interpret art or design that shows how people around the world live and what matters to them, and analyze how visual parts and cultural links sway ideas, feelings and actions. What changes: the student analyzes how visual parts and cultural links sway ideas, feelings and actions, where grade 5 only found the links. Assessed by a written response using look-describe-interpret with evidence from the image, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: audience; display; location; value; sway; image
notes: Explain how the way a work is displayed, where it is and the viewer's own experience change how it is seen and valued, and analyze several ways images sway different audiences. What changes: display and audience join the picture as things that change meaning. Assessed by a written response using look-describe-interpret with evidence from the image, scored on a short rubric.

words: taste; culture; setting; media; sway; image
notes: Explain how culture and surroundings shape a person's taste and image, and compare the settings and media where viewers meet images that try to sway them. What changes: settings and media are compared, where grade 7 looked at audiences. Assessed by a written response using look-describe-interpret with evidence from the image, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: perceive; experience; image; view; analyze; world
notes: Propose ways art shapes how people see and understand human experience, and analyze how seeing images shapes the student's own view of the world. What changes: the student looks at their own seeing, where grade 8 compared settings. Assessed by a written response with evidence from the image and its setting, scored on a rubric for evidence and reasoning.

words: taste; surroundings; audience; judge; image; feeling
notes: Notice and describe your own feelings and tastes toward nature and built surroundings, and judge how well images sway the ideas, feelings and actions of particular audiences. What changes: the student judges how well an image works on its audience, where level 1 analyzed how images shape a viewer. Assessed by a written response with evidence from the image and its setting, scored on a rubric for evidence and reasoning.

words: reaction; growth; pattern; era; type; share
notes: Analyze how a reaction to art grows with learning and life experience, and find what artists or images of one type, era or culture have in common. What changes: patterns across a type, era or culture are found, where level 2 judged single images. Assessed by a written response with evidence from the image and its setting, scored on a rubric for evidence and reasoning. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: subject; detail; prefer; because; meaning; like
notes: Work out an artwork's meaning by naming its subject and describing key details, and tell why the child prefers a certain artwork. Use the sentence 'I like it because'. What changes: first judging: name a subject and key details, and say why you prefer one work. Assessed by a talk: the child says which work they prefer and why, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: subject; form; sort; reason; feature; prefer
notes: Work out an artwork's meaning by sorting subject matter and naming features of form, and sort artwork by the different reasons people like it. What changes: features of form are named and several reasons for liking a work are sorted, where kindergarten gave one reason. Assessed by a talk: the child says which work they prefer and why, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: mood; subject; form; prefer; art word; meaning
notes: Find an artwork's meaning from the mood it suggests, its subject and its form, and use art words to say which work the child prefers. What changes: mood joins subject and form as a source of meaning, where grade 1 sorted by subject and features of form. Assessed by a talk: the child says which work they prefer and why, marked as met, partly or not yet.

words: media; mood; standard; judge; given; meaning
notes: Work out meaning by studying how media build subject, form and mood, and judge an artwork using standards given by the teacher. What changes: standards given by the teacher are applied for the first time, where grade 2 gave a preference in art words. Assessed by a short response that gives a reason and uses art words, scored on a three-line guide.

words: background; context; standard; judge; compare; meaning
notes: Find an artwork's meaning using background facts and a look at subject, form and media, and use one set of standards to judge more than one artwork. What changes: background facts feed the meaning, and one set of standards is used on more than one work. Assessed by a short response that gives a reason and uses art words, scored on a three-line guide.

words: structure; context; genre; standard; culture; mood
notes: Find ideas and mood in an artwork by studying form, structure, context, subject and media, and describe how standards for judging art shift with style, genre, history and culture. What changes: the student describes how standards for judging art change with style, history and culture. Assessed by a short response that gives a reason and uses art words, scored on a three-line guide.

words: context; evidence; standard; create; judge; useful
cross_subject: ela:W.6.1 (a claim with reasons and evidence)
notes: Sort useful from unhelpful context before studying a work, and create and use fitting standards to judge an artwork. What changes: the student creates standards and uses an evidence sentence. Assessed by a response that judges a work against stated standards with evidence, scored on a short rubric.

words: taste; standard; weigh; making; evidence; judge
notes: Find meaning by weighing a work's making, form, structure, context, subject and media, and compare and explain how judging by personal taste differs from judging by established standards. What changes: personal taste and established standards are told apart, where grade 6 made standards for a work. Assessed by a response that judges a work against stated standards with evidence, scored on a short rubric.

words: argue; reasons; judgment; context; structure; message
cross_subject: ela:W.8.1 (an argument supported by reasons and evidence)
notes: Study how subject, form, structure, media, approach and context together build messages and mood, and argue with solid reasons for a judgment of an artwork. What changes: the judgment is argued in writing with solid reasons, where grade 7 compared taste and standards. Assessed by a response that judges a work against stated standards with evidence, scored on a short rubric.

words: evidence; context; standards; collection; explain; cite
notes: Explain an artwork's meaning, citing enough evidence from the piece and its contexts, and set fitting standards for judging an artwork or collection. What changes: evidence is counted for enough, and the student sets standards for a work or collection. Assessed by a written judgment that sets standards, applies them and gives evidence, scored on a rubric.

words: background; interpretation; source; standards; fit; decide
notes: Name the kinds of background information that help build interpretations of art, and decide how well other people's judging standards fit an artwork or collection. What changes: other people's standards are tested against a work, and background that helps interpretation is named. Assessed by a written judgment that sets standards, applies them and gives evidence, scored on a rubric.

words: interpretation; compete; defend; believable; standards; judgment
notes: Analyze competing interpretations of art to choose and defend the most believable, and build judgments of an artwork or collection using several different sets of standards. What changes: competing interpretations are weighed against each other and several sets of standards are used in one judgment. Assessed by a written judgment that sets standards, applies them and gives evidence, scored on a rubric.

model_in: sketchbook; safe-studio; practice-log; talk-about-choices; critique-protocol; artist-statement
model_out: sketchbook; safe-studio; practice-log; talk-about-choices; critique-protocol; artist-statement
words: self-directed; series; proposal; studio; revision; portfolio
notes: Level 4 is an optional year the student leads: a self-directed series built from a written proposal, with planning, making and revision repeated on new work. Assessed by a portfolio of the series and a defended artist statement, scored on the same rubric as Level 3 with a higher bar for independence. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to new, self-chosen work.

words: liberty; duty; image; culture; society; project
notes: The student takes on one project that uses art or design to speak to a real audience, and keeps a record of choices about materials, sources, consent and sharing. Assessed by the finished project and a written account of its ethical choices. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to a new project.

words: curate; exhibit; justify; conservation; society; catalogue
notes: The student curates and presents a small public exhibit from the Level 4 work, writing a justified label for each piece and a plan for protecting the work. Assessed by the exhibition, the labels and a short talk to visitors, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: a showing outside class needs each family's yes. A student of 18 or over gives their own yes to be shown; otherwise the family does. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11.

words: interpretation; criticism; compare; believable; standards; evidence
cross_subject: ela:W.11-12.1 (an argument with valid reasoning and evidence)
notes: The student writes an extended critical essay comparing the interpretations of a work or group of works, defending the most believable one with evidence and more than one set of standards. Assessed by the essay and a defended talk, scored on a rubric. The Level 3 ids are owned in grade 11; this year applies them to new works.

words: beat; high; low; sound; motif; move
notes: Explore beat and the shape of a tune by moving, singing and tapping, then invent short motifs from movement. Ideas go into a first idea bank, a bundle of recordings or picture cards. What changes: first year: beat and tune shape are felt by moving, singing and tapping, and a first motif is invented. Assessed by a music-making check: the teacher marks each child's tries as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: the child's voice is never forced; a clap, a tap or a found sound counts.

words: favorite; pick; picture symbol; record; order; idea
notes: Pick favorite musical ideas and keep them with picture symbols or a recording. What changes: first year: ideas are picked and kept, not yet explained. Assessed by a kept-ideas check: the teacher marks each child's picked and kept ideas as met, partly or not yet.

words: feedback; improve; share; classmates; finished; again
notes: Use help from self, peers and teacher to improve a musical idea, then play a finished version for classmates. What changes: first year: one idea is improved with help and played for classmates. Assessed by a sharing check: the teacher marks the change and the sharing as met, partly or not yet.

words: high; low; loud; soft; same; different
notes: Notice high and low, loud and soft, and same and different in songs, and show each with the body. What changes: first year: high and low, loud and soft, and same and different are shown with the body, with no notation. Assessed by a listening game: the teacher marks each child's body answers as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: beat counts and body answers only, no note values.

words: loud; soft; fast; slow; voice; mean
notes: Notice how voice, loudness and speed support what a creator means, and notice the same in what performers do. What changes: first year: voice, loudness and speed are noticed as carriers of what a maker means. Assessed by a listen-and-show check: the teacher marks each child's answers as met, partly or not yet.

words: practice; again; feedback; expressive; audience; sing
notes: Use help from self, teacher and peers to improve a performance, try suggested ways to practice, and perform expressively for an audience such as the class. What changes: first year: a performance is improved with help and given to an audience such as the class. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher marks each child's performance as met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: volume stays low, no child is made to sing alone, and a group or recorded version is always an option.

words: favorite; like; choose; why; song; interest
notes: Show and say what interests you in different music, list interests and experiences, and show why some music is a favorite. What changes: first year: what interests a child is shown and said. Assessed by a favorites check: the teacher marks each child's show-and-say as met, partly or not yet.

words: beat; tune; like; judge; art; school
notes: Show how a music idea such as beat or tune direction is used, judge music by taste, and show how music meets other arts, school subjects and daily life. What changes: first year: a music idea is shown and a taste is stated. Assessed by a listen-and-say check: the teacher marks each child's answers as met, partly or not yet.

words: reply; phrase; purpose; major; minor; twos and threes
notes: Make a reply phrase for a purpose such as a greeting or a goodnight, and try ideas that sound happy or sad and that move in twos or threes. What changes: a purpose for each idea and a first try at different tonalities and meters. Assessed by a music-making check: the teacher marks each child's phrases as met, partly or not yet.

words: choose; reason; notation; recording; picture symbols; express
notes: Play ideas chosen to express an intent, say why they were chosen, and document them in picture or standard notation or in a recording. What changes: the child gives a reason and documents the idea. Assessed by a kept-ideas check: the teacher marks the reason and the record as met, partly or not yet.

words: feedback; polish; purpose; meaning; share; change
notes: Use feedback from self, peers and teacher to polish an idea, and share finished music with classmates, showing its purpose and meaning. What changes: the child polishes with less help and says what the music is for. Assessed by a sharing check: the teacher marks the change and the purpose as met, partly or not yet.

words: beat; melody direction; picture notation; rhythm; culture; pattern
notes: Show the beat and which way a tune moves in music from many cultures, and read and perform short rhythm patterns in picture or standard notation. Beat counts and picture symbols only, no note values. What changes: reading begins with simple rhythm patterns from picture symbols. Assessed by a read-and-play task scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: music from a culture is chosen from that community's own published teaching or a named practitioner. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: loudness; speed; express; creator; performer; show
notes: Show and describe how music expresses itself through loudness and speed, and name how these reflect what creators and performers mean. What changes: the child names how loudness and speed carry what a creator means, where kindergarten only noticed them. Assessed by a listen-and-show check scored on a three-line guide.

words: rehearse; strategy; expressive; purpose; audience; feedback
notes: Use feedback from self, teacher and peers to improve a performance, try a suggested rehearsal strategy on a hard spot, and perform expressively in a way that fits both the audience and the purpose. What changes: less help, and a performance fitted to an audience and a purpose. Assessed by a performance check: the teacher marks each child's performance as met, partly or not yet.

words: interest; purpose; experience; choose; skill; knowledge
notes: Show and discuss interest in varied music and its purpose, show how interests and experiences shape music choices for purposes, and show how tastes, knowledge and skills shape choices and aims. What changes: choices are tied to a purpose for the music, where kindergarten only showed interest. Assessed by a favorites check with one spoken reason, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: beat; pitch; purpose; style; judge; connect
notes: Show how beat or pitch serve a purpose in varied styles, judge music for a purpose by taste and expression, and show how music relates to other arts, school subjects and daily life. What changes: the child names a purpose that beat or pitch serves, where kindergarten only showed an idea. Assessed by a listen-and-say check, marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: improvise; pattern; rhythm; melody; tonality; meter
notes: Improvise rhythm and melody patterns for a purpose, then make patterns inside a tonality and meter the teacher gives. What changes: improvising on purpose and working inside a given tonality and meter. Assessed by a performance of two patterns scored on a three-line guide.

words: combine; sequence; document; notation; recording; order
notes: Show and explain why patterns were chosen, then document, combine and sequence ideas in picture or standard notation or a recording. What changes: ideas are combined and put in order, not only kept one by one. Assessed by a documented short piece scored on a three-line guide.

words: feedback; revise; sense; mean; for; share
notes: Make sense of feedback from self, peers and teacher and revise the music, then share finished music with classmates, showing what it means and what it is for. What changes: the child decides which feedback to use. Assessed by a revised piece and a one-line note on the change, scored on a three-line guide.

words: tonality; meter; major; minor; rhythm pattern; melody pattern
notes: Show tonality and meter in music from many cultures chosen for performance, and read and perform rhythm and melody patterns in picture or standard notation. Rhythms are taught by beat counts and a spoken counting system. What changes: tonality and meter are named, and melody patterns are read as well as rhythms. Assessed by a read-and-play task scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: tempo; dynamics; concept; intent; creator; performer
notes: Show how creators use loudness, speed and other qualities to express intent, and how music concepts serve what creators and performers intend. What changes: qualities beyond loudness and speed are tied to a creator's intent. Assessed by a performance and a spoken reason scored on a three-line guide.

words: criteria; accurate; expressive; effective; strategy; rehearse
notes: Use set criteria to judge how accurate, expressive and effective performances are, choose and use rehearsal strategies for hard spots, and perform expressively and accurately for a purpose. What changes: the child chooses the strategy and judges with set criteria. Assessed by a performance scored on a three-line guide (accurate, expressive, fits the purpose).

words: interest; purpose; explain; choose; knowledge; varied
notes: Show and explain interest in, knowledge of and purpose for varied music, explain how interests and experiences shape music choices, and show how tastes and skills shape choices and aims. What changes: the child explains a choice in words, where grade 1 showed and discussed it. Assessed by a short spoken or written reason scored on a three-line guide.

words: concept; purpose; judge; taste; connect; subject
notes: Describe how music concepts serve a particular purpose, judge music for a purpose by taste and expression, and show how music relates to other arts, school subjects and daily life. What changes: the child describes how a music concept serves a purpose, where grade 1 only showed it. Assessed by a short listen-and-describe response scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: improvise; setting; purpose; choose; fits; tonality
notes: Improvise rhythm and melody ideas, say how they fit a purpose and a setting, then invent ideas in a tonality or meter the child chooses. What changes: the child explains the fit and chooses the tonality or meter. Assessed by a performance and a spoken reason scored on a short rubric.

words: piece; purpose; rhythm; melody; standard notation; picture notation
notes: Play chosen ideas as a simple improvised or composed piece linked to its purpose, and document the rhythm and melody in standard or picture notation or a recording. What changes: ideas become a piece with a stated purpose. Assessed by a documented piece scored on a short rubric.

words: criteria; judge; record; changes; audience; intent
notes: Judge and improve musical ideas with teacher and class criteria, record the changes, and share finished music with an audience, describing how it shows the child's intent. What changes: class criteria guide the changes and an audience hears the result. Assessed by a revised piece with a recorded change list, scored on a short rubric.

words: structure; section; rhythm; short tune; notation; context
cross_subject: math:3.NF.A.1 (a note value is a part of a whole bar)
notes: Show the structure of music chosen for performance, read and perform rhythms and short tunes in picture and standard notation, and describe how personal and social setting can shape a performance. Note values are placed after the unit on fractions as parts of a whole. What changes: whole tunes are read in picture and standard notation, and the setting of a performance is described. Assessed by a read-and-play task and a spoken description of the setting, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: reading; interpret; loudness; speed; intent; performer
notes: Describe and show how loudness and speed carry intent across, and describe how performers use them in their readings to show intent. What changes: the child compares readings by different performers, where grade 2 named qualities in one. Assessed by a performance and a short description scored on a short rubric.

words: ensemble; criteria; polish; manners; audience; venue
notes: Use class criteria and feedback to judge how accurate ensemble performances are, rehearse to polish accuracy and expression, and perform with the manners of a performer and an audience member that suit the venue. What changes: ensemble work, class criteria and audience manners. Assessed by a performance and a self-check scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: a solo or doubled version is always offered.

words: setting; purpose; choose; reflect; knowledge; audience
notes: Show how interests, knowledge, purpose and setting influence choosing music to perform, describe how chosen music reflects interests, experiences and purposes, and show how tastes and skills shape choices. What changes: setting joins interest and purpose as a reason for choosing music to perform. Assessed by a listening-log entry with a reason scored on a short rubric.

words: structure; element; setting; criteria; fit; connect
cross_subject: ela:SL.3.1 (class talk about what was heard)
notes: Describe how structure, music elements and personal or social setting shape responses to music, judge pieces and performances by set criteria, describe fit to the setting, and show how music relates to other arts, subjects and daily life. What changes: set criteria and the personal or social setting enter the judging, where grade 2 judged by taste and expression. Assessed by a listen-and-describe response scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: harmony; accompaniment; related; explain; setting; drone
notes: Improvise rhythm, melody and a simple harmony part, explain how the ideas fit their purpose and setting, and invent a simple accompaniment in related tonalities and meters. What changes: harmony and accompaniment join rhythm and melody. Assessed by a performance with a spoken reason, scored on a short rubric.

words: arrange; compose; organized; context; harmony; notation
notes: Play ideas chosen and organized for improvising, arranging or composing, say what each is for, and write down rhythm, melody and a simple harmony part. What changes: organizing and explaining join documenting, and simple harmony is written down, where grade 3 documented one melody. Assessed by a documented piece and a spoken or written reason, scored on a rubric.

words: growth; shared criteria; revise; record; audience; explain
notes: Revise and record changes to music against shared criteria, showing growth over time, and share finished music with an audience, explaining how it shows intent. What changes: changes are kept over time and shown as growth, where grade 3 kept a change list. Assessed by a portfolio entry with before and after versions, scored on a rubric.

words: timing; pitch; form; time signature; notation; culture
cross_subject: math:4.NF.A.1 (equal note values, such as two quarters in one half)
notes: Show how timing, pitch and form work in music chosen to perform, read and perform music in picture or standard notation, and explain how social and cultural setting shapes a performance. Equal note values are shown as equal parts of a bar. What changes: elements are named and explained, and setting is explained rather than described. Assessed by a read-and-play task and a short explanation scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: interpretive choice; tone color; loudness; speed; intent; explain
notes: Show and explain how interpretive choices, loudness, speed and tone color put intent across, in the child's own performing and in performers heard. What changes: tone color joins loudness and speed, and explaining replaces describing. Assessed by a performance and a spoken reason scored on a rubric.

words: solo; group; shared criteria; interpretation; genre; manners
notes: Use shared criteria to judge group and solo performances, rehearse to sharpen correctness and expression, and play or sing solo or in a group with fitting interpretation and manners that suit the setting, venue and genre. What changes: interpretation is tied to the genre, where grade 3 tied manners to the venue. Assessed by a performance and a self-check scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: a solo or doubled version is always offered.

words: technical skill; setting; context; reflect; choose; explain
notes: Show how interests, knowledge, setting and technical skill influence choosing music to perform, explain how chosen music reflects interests, experiences, purposes and contexts, and show how tastes and skills shape choices. What changes: the child's own technical skill is a reason for choosing, where grade 3 weighed setting. Assessed by a listening-log entry with a reason scored on a short rubric.

words: structure; element; culture; criteria; explain; connect
notes: Describe how structure, music elements and social or cultural setting shape responses, judge pieces and performances by set criteria and explain their fit to the setting, and show how music relates to other arts, subjects and daily life. What changes: explaining replaces describing: the child says why the setting changes the response. Assessed by a listen-and-explain response scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: context; culture; history; chords; accompaniment; society
notes: Improvise rhythm, melody and harmony, explain the tie between the ideas and a social, cultural or historical setting, and invent an accompaniment with easy chords. What changes: ideas are tied to a social, cultural or historical setting, and easy chords back them. Assessed by a performance and a short explanation with one piece of evidence, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: developed; two-chord; arrange; context; notation; recording
notes: Play ideas chosen and developed for improvising, arranging or composing, say what each is for, and write down rhythm, melody and a two-chord harmony. What changes: ideas are developed further and a two-chord harmony is written, where grade 4 wrote a simple harmony part. Assessed by a documented piece scored on a rubric for development and clear notation.

words: reasons; criteria; revise; well-crafted; audience; growth
notes: Revise and record changes to music against shared criteria, explain the reasons, and share well-crafted finished music with an audience, explaining how it shows intent. What changes: the child explains why each change was made. Assessed by a portfolio entry with before and after versions and reasons, scored on a rubric.

words: harmony; timing; pitch; form; staff; notation
cross_subject: math:5.NF.A.1 (adding mixed note values within a bar)
notes: Show how timing, pitch, form and harmony work in a piece chosen to perform, and read and perform it from standard notation. Mixed note values are added within a bar. What changes: harmony joins the elements and standard notation is now the default, where grade 4 used picture or standard notation. Assessed by a read-and-play task and a written explanation scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: articulation; tone color; interpretive choice; intent; explain; performer
notes: Explain how interpretive choices, loudness, speed, tone color and articulation put intent across, in the child's performing and in performers heard. What changes: articulation joins the qualities explained, where grade 4 explained tone color. Assessed by a performance and a written explanation scored on a rubric.

words: growth; criteria; genre; style; interpretation; venue
notes: Use teacher-set criteria to judge accuracy and expression, rehearse to sharpen correctness and expression and show growth over time, and perform solo or in a group with manners that suit style, genre, venue and setting. What changes: growth over time is shown across rehearsals with a log, where grade 4 judged by shared criteria. Assessed by a performance and a rehearsal log scored on a rubric. Teacher note: a solo or doubled version is always offered.

words: evidence; interest; skill; setting; context; choose
notes: Show how interest, knowledge, setting, and the child's and others' skill guide choosing music to perform, explain with evidence how chosen music reflects interests, experiences, purposes and contexts, and show how tastes and skills shape choices. What changes: claims come with evidence from the music. Assessed by a listening-log entry with evidence scored on a rubric.

words: evidence; history; culture; criteria; setting; connect
cross_subject: ela:W.5.1 (an opinion supported by reasons)
notes: Give evidence from the music for how structure, elements and a social, cultural or historical setting shape a response, judge pieces and performances by set criteria, citing evidence from the music elements for fit to the setting, explain how history, culture and society shape a performance, and show how music relates to other arts, school subjects, settings and daily life. What changes: evidence from the music is required, in the response and in the judgment, and the setting of a performance is tied to history and society. Assessed by a written response with evidence scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: phrase; AB form; ABA form; intent; harmony; chord
notes: Make simple rhythm, melody and harmony phrases in AB or ABA form that express a chosen intent. What changes: phrases are shaped into AB or ABA form to carry an intent. Assessed by a short composed piece scored on a rubric for form and intent.

words: AB form; ABA form; beginning; middle; end; two chords
notes: Write down ideas as AB or ABA pieces with a clear start, middle and finish, using two-chord ideas and simple rhythm and melody phrases. What changes: pieces have a planned shape from start to finish, where grade 5 documented developed ideas. Assessed by a documented piece scored on a rubric for shape and clear notation or audio.

words: criteria; sound source; music element; revise; craft; originality
notes: Judge a piece against teacher criteria such as chosen music elements and sound sources, explain why it was revised using the teacher's feedback, and present a documented arrangement or composition with craft and originality. What changes: the student judges the piece and presents a whole documented piece. Assessed by a presented piece and a revision note scored on a rubric for craft, originality and reasons.

words: dynamics; articulation; pitch; rhythm; symbol; culture
notes: Explain how structure and elements work in a piece chosen to perform, read and name the standard symbols for dynamics, articulation, pitch and rhythm, and say how the piece's culture and history shape its performance. What changes: symbols are read and named one by one, where grade 5 read notation without naming each symbol. Assessed by a symbol-reading task and a written note on the piece, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: interpretation; genre; history; elements; expression; intent
notes: Perform a chosen piece, showing how the student's interpretation of elements and expression conveys intent, and describe a reading of how elements and expression, within genre and history, convey intent. What changes: the student makes interpretive choices alone and describes them, where grade 5 explained choices made together. Assessed by a performance and a written description scored on a rubric.

words: ready; criteria; creator; intent; stage presence; dress
notes: Use teacher criteria to rehearse, polish and decide when a piece is ready, and perform it accurately to carry out the creator's intent, showing manners such as dress and stage presence that fit the venue. What changes: the student decides when a piece is ready. Assessed by a performance and a readiness note scored on a rubric.

words: criteria; choose; purpose; setting; interest; experience
notes: Use teacher criteria to pick music for a purpose or setting and explain each pick, choose music for a purpose and explain its tie to the student's interests or experiences, and show how tastes and skills shape choices. What changes: teacher criteria guide each pick, where grade 5 chose by evidence from the music. Assessed by a listening-log entry with a reason scored on a rubric.

words: genre; era; setting; structure; teacher criteria; connect
cross_subject: ela:SL.6.1 (discussion with evidence)
notes: Describe how elements and expression connect to a piece's structure, name the setting of music from many genres, cultures and eras, use teacher criteria to judge pieces or performances, and show how music relates to other arts, subjects and daily life. What changes: settings are named across genres, cultures and eras, where grade 5 cited one setting. Assessed by a written response scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: variation; theme; chord progression; phrase; contrast; form
notes: Build varied phrases over a chord pattern in AB, ABA or variation-on-a-theme form. What changes: phrases grow over chords and may vary a theme. Assessed by a short composed piece scored on a rubric for form, variety and fit with the chords.

words: unity; variety; variation; chord sequence; notation; audio
notes: Organize and document ideas in AB, ABA or variation forms that show both unity and variety, with simple rhythm phrases, melody phrases and chord sequences. What changes: unity and variety are named and shown. Assessed by a documented piece scored on a rubric for unity, variety and clear documentation.

words: style; form; criteria; feedback; unity; variety
notes: Judge the student's own work against chosen criteria such as style, form and sound sources, explain revisions with the criteria and peer and teacher feedback, and present a documented song, arrangement or composition with unity and variety. What changes: the student chooses the criteria for judging own work, where grade 6 used the teacher's. Assessed by a presented piece and a revision note scored on a rubric for criteria, reasons, unity and variety.

words: tempo; form; dynamics; reading; contrast; culture
notes: Show and explain how contrasting performance pieces are built and how their elements work, read and name standard symbols for form, tempo, dynamics, articulation, pitch and rhythm, and name how culture and history lead to different readings of a piece. What changes: two contrasting pieces and more symbols, including form and tempo. Assessed by a symbol-reading task and a written comparison, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: contrast; interpretation; elements; expression; intent; reading
notes: Perform contrasting pieces, showing the student's own interpretation of elements and expression, and describe a reading of contrasting works, explaining how they convey intent. What changes: two contrasting works are interpreted and compared. Assessed by a two-piece performance and a written comparison scored on a rubric.

words: ready; class criteria; style; creator; intent; venue
notes: Use class-made criteria to rehearse, polish and decide when music is ready, and perform it accurately and in style to carry out the creator's intent, with manners that fit the context, purpose and venue. What changes: the class makes the criteria and style is added to accuracy. Assessed by a performance and a readiness note scored on a rubric.

words: contrast; program; shared criteria; compare; interest; choose
notes: Use shared criteria to choose contrasting music for a program and discuss why, compare each piece's tie to the student's interests, and show how tastes and skills shape choices. What changes: contrasting pieces are compared for a program, where grade 6 picked one piece at a time. Assessed by a short program note scored on a rubric.

words: sort; compare; setting; teacher criteria; contrast; connect
notes: Sort and explain how elements and expression relate to how contrasting pieces are built, name and compare the setting of music from many genres, cultures and eras, choose from teacher criteria to judge pieces or performances, and show how music relates to other arts, subjects and daily life. What changes: the student sorts, compares and chooses among criteria, where grade 6 used the teacher's. Assessed by a written comparison scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: introduction; transition; coda; expanded form; accompaniment; section
notes: Build phrases and accompaniments in an expanded form with an introduction, transitions and a coda. What changes: forms expand with an introduction, transitions and a coda. Assessed by a composed piece scored on a rubric for form, link between sections and accompaniment. Teacher note: high school music is a separate composition and theory strand, so no row hands on from grade 8.

words: tension; release; balance; expanded form; unity; variety
