notes: Organize and document ideas in expanded forms that balance tension, unity, variety and release, with rhythm phrases, melody phrases and chord sequences. What changes: tension and release are planned and balanced in a longer form. Assessed by a documented piece scored on a rubric for balance and clear documentation.

words: technique; justify; polish; tension; release; balance
notes: Judge the student's own work by choosing criteria such as technique, style, form and sound sources, justify the polish against those criteria, and present a documented piece that uses composing techniques for unity, variety, tension, release and balance. What changes: the student justifies each choice against criteria. Assessed by a presented piece and a written justification scored on a rubric.

words: sight-read; treble staff; bass staff; compare; build; effect
notes: Compare how contrasting performance pieces are built and how elements work in each, sight-read simple rhythm, melody or harmony notation on treble or bass staves, and name how culture and history create different effects in performance. What changes: the student reads new notation at sight on treble or bass staves, where grade 7 read familiar pieces. Assessed by a sight-reading task and a written comparison, scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: program; reading; back; evidence; interpretation; convey
notes: Perform contrasting pieces and explain how the student's interpretation conveys the music's intent, and back a reading of contrasting programs with evidence about how elements and expression convey intent. What changes: readings are backed with evidence across a whole program. Assessed by a performance and a written argument with evidence, scored on a rubric.

words: own criteria; style; culturally authentic; honor; venue; ready
notes: Use the student's own criteria to rehearse, polish and decide when music is ready, and perform it accurately, in style and with culturally authentic practice that honors the creator's intent, with manners that fit style, context, purpose and venue. What changes: the student writes the criteria and authentic practice is added. Assessed by a performance and a readiness note scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: program; own criteria; mix; select; interest; contrast
notes: Use the student's own criteria to choose contrasting music for a program and explain why, select a program such as a mix and show its tie to the student's interests, and show how tastes and skills shape choices. What changes: the student sets the criteria and builds a program. Assessed by a program note scored on a rubric.

words: program; compare; own criteria; setting; evidence; connect
cross_subject: ela:W.8.1 (an argument supported by evidence)
notes: Compare how elements and expression connect to structure across whole music programs, name and compare the setting of programs from many genres, cultures and eras, use criteria the student made to judge pieces or performances, and show how music relates to other arts, subjects and daily life. What changes: whole programs are compared and the student writes the criteria, where grade 7 compared pairs of pieces. Assessed by a written argument with evidence scored on a rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: pretend; imagine; place; idea; question; share
notes: With help, invent and enter an imagined place in pretend play, share an original idea, and ask and answer questions along the way. What changes: first year, pretend play led by a grown-up guide. Assessed by a short teacher-recorded observation of pretend play, said aloud or shown, marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: pretend play only, with a safe clear space; no one is made to play a role they do not want.

words: together; turn; join; add; pretend; friend
notes: Join classmates in pretend play, add an idea of your own to it, and take an active turn in the group. What changes: first year, taking turns and joining in. Assessed by a short group showing with the teacher's mark of met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: a child may watch first and join in later.

words: voice; sound; loud; quiet; pretend; play
cross_subject: ela:SL.K.6 (speak clearly to say what you mean)
notes: With help, see that sound and your voice are basic to pretend play, and use voice and sounds in it. What changes: first year, the voice and sounds as tools. Assessed by a short voice and movement showing marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: voice rest and no forced loud sounds; falls and contact are not rehearsed.

words: puppet; prop; costume; make; sound; light
notes: With help, craft puppets, props and costume bits from simple materials, and try out simple sound and light elements in pretend play. What changes: first year, making things for pretend play. Assessed by a made prop or puppet and a spoken reason, marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: found, safe materials only; no hot lights or sharp tools.

words: character; place; story; tale; act out; beginning
cross_subject: ela:RL.K.3 (a story has characters, settings and events)
notes: Hear a short tale, point out who the characters are and where it happens, tell two tales apart, and act out one brief tale with help. What changes: first year, who and where in a short tale. Assessed by a retelling or short scene marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: like me; feeling; skill; subject; character; play
notes: With help, spot likenesses between characters and yourself, and name skills from other subjects that show up in pretend play. What changes: first year, how a character is like me. Assessed by a spoken line that ties a character to the child's life, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: like; feel; character; favorite; prefer; show
notes: With help, share how you feel about characters and name preferences in pretend play or guided drama. What changes: first year, saying what I like and how it feels. Assessed by a spoken reaction with a reason, marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: a child may point or draw instead of saying it.

words: character; choice; gesture; movement; plot; step
notes: In guided drama, suggest what a character might choose to do, show with gestures and movement how a tale is told, and add the next step to a plot built in order. What changes: children suggest choices and build a plot in order, not only play along. Assessed by a short teacher-recorded observation of pretend play, said aloud or shown, marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide.

words: decide; group; change; plot; build; idea
notes: With help, join group decisions, help change the plot, and build on classmates' ideas in guided drama. What changes: children help decide and change the story, not only join in. Assessed by a short group showing with the teacher's mark of met, partly or not yet.

words: face; body; gesture; feeling; voice; move
notes: In guided drama, show a character's traits and feelings with face, body, gesture and voice, and compare how sounds and movements are alike and different. What changes: face, body and gesture show feelings and traits. Assessed by a short voice and movement showing marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: clear floor space, no contact, and no falls.

words: costume; prop; plan; stand for; tech; object
notes: Plan costumes and props with classmates, name the tech elements you could use, find ways one object can stand for another, and name what you might bring in. What changes: children plan before making and name the tech elements. Assessed by a made prop or puppet and a spoken reason, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: cause; action; scene; community; fiction; alike
cross_subject: ela:RL.1.3 (describe characters, settings and events)
notes: Describe what a character does and says and why, notice how stories from your own community are alike and unlike, and make a short scene together from a fiction source. What changes: causes of actions and stories from the child's own community. Assessed by a retelling or short scene marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: feeling; life; art; subject; character; know
notes: Name a character's feelings and tie them to your own life, and bring what you know from other arts and subjects into guided drama. What changes: feelings are tied to the child's own life. Assessed by a spoken line that ties a character to the child's life, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: remember; choice; prefer; feeling; compare; experience
notes: Remember the choices made in guided drama, say what you prefer and how it felt, and use words or pictures to compare your choices with a character's. What changes: the child remembers choices and compares self with a character. Assessed by a spoken reaction with a reason, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: detail; voice; sound; dialogue; plot; invent
notes: In guided drama, add new details to the plot and story, find ways voice and sounds tell a tale, and make up dialogue with classmates. What changes: voice and sound join movement, and dialogue is made up together. Assessed by a short teacher-recorded observation of pretend play, said aloud or shown, marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide.

words: scene; dialogue; share; together; story; audience
notes: Decide with classmates how to move the story on, help change the dialogue, work on a scene together, and share it informally with the class. What changes: a scene is shared with classmates for the first time. Assessed by a short group showing with the teacher's mark of met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: a friendly showing for the class; a solo or recorded version is always offered.

words: sound; move; adjust; mind; subtle; character
cross_subject: ela:SL.2.4 (tell a story aloud so it can be heard and followed)
notes: Change your voice and movement to show small differences in a character, notice how body, mind and voice work together, and adjust sounds and moves as you go. What changes: sound and movement are adjusted to show small differences in a character. Assessed by a short voice and movement showing marked met, partly or not yet.

words: scenery; prop; costume; tech; stand for; place
notes: With classmates, plan scenery, try out tech elements, think alone of many ways for one object to stand for another, and show a character, place or event with a costume or prop. What changes: scenery joins props and costumes, and a prop shows a place or event. Assessed by a made prop or puppet and a spoken reason, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: cause; result; culture; nonfiction; scene; part
notes: Say what the parts of a story mean, name the causes and results of characters' actions, compare stories from several cultures, and make a short scene from a nonfiction source. What changes: results join causes and stories come from several cultures. Assessed by a retelling or short scene marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: experience; relate; art; subject; pick; fit
notes: Relate characters' experiences to your own, and pick which know-how from other arts and subjects suits the drama. What changes: the child chooses which outside know-how fits. Assessed by a spoken line that ties a character to the child's life, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: decide; taste; reaction; compare; problem; handle
notes: Spot the moments when artists decide things, say how your own tastes and feelings shape your reaction, and compare how characters handle problems with your own choices. What changes: the child spots the decision moments and how others feel. Assessed by a spoken reaction with a reason, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: improvise; setting; character; method; group; idea
notes: Make up characters, imagined settings and improvised stories, decide as a group how characters could move and talk, and try an idea-finding method of your own for a drama work. What changes: children make up whole characters and settings and try a method for finding ideas. Assessed by an idea sheet and a short spoken or written reason, scored on a three-line rubric. Teacher note: no real weapons or contact, and no character is played by accent or stereotype.

words: rehearse; limit; compare; reflect; group; strengthen
notes: Compare ideas with classmates and keep those that strengthen the group's piece, rework ideas to fit set limits, then rehearse and reflect alone and with a few classmates. What changes: rehearsal and reflection become steps, with limits to work inside. Assessed by a rehearsed showing and a critique-and-revise note, scored on a short rubric for preparation, role and revision.

words: exercise; movement; voice; body; explore; character
notes: Take part in sets of body, voice and thinking exercises and look at how drama work uses movement and voice, then explore both for scripted or unscripted scenes. What changes: exercises come in sets for body, voice and thinking. Assessed by a short performance and a self-check, scored on a short rubric for voice, body and a clear character.

words: set; costume; prop; tech element; design; decision
notes: Describe costume, prop and set ideas that suit a story's setting and characters, name basic tech elements, polish design decisions in rehearsal, and compare tech elements in several works. What changes: design ideas must suit the setting and are polished in rehearsal. Assessed by a design sketch or model with a written reason, scored on a short rubric for fit to the story and care in making.

words: structure; beginning; middle; end; convention; retell
cross_subject: ela:RL.3.3 (how a character's actions move the story)
notes: Build a piece from the parts of dramatic structure, turn a written story into a stage piece, and look at how artists of the past retold stories. What changes: a written story is reshaped into a stage piece using structure. Assessed by a short written or staged response about one story, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: community; culture; social problem; subject; costume; view
notes: Draw on what you know and have lived to connect with community and culture, spot how drama work connects to community life, social problems and other subjects, and weigh ways to build a character with looks, props and costumes that show cultural views. What changes: community and culture enter the work. Assessed by a short written or spoken response naming one community tie and one other-subject tie, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: the child's own community is the starting point, and no child speaks for a whole group. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: reason; decision; experience; connect; feeling; watch
notes: Look for the reasons behind artists' decisions in a drama piece, name several of your own experiences from joining in or watching, and say how you connect with a character's feelings. What changes: reasons behind decisions are sought and the child's experiences are named. Assessed by an audience-journal entry citing one choice an artist made, scored on a three-line guide.

words: judge; group; audience; problem; situation; reason
notes: Say why and how groups judge a drama piece, and judge a play's problems and situations from an audience member's seat. What changes: judging becomes its own thread: why groups judge, and how an audience sees. Assessed by a short response to a showing with a reason, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: judging is of the work, never of the maker.

words: given circumstances; world; question; improvise; invent; plot
notes: Describe how an imagined world looks and how an improvised story fits its given circumstances, picture how a character moves to fit them, and question characters and plots to invent ideas. What changes: given circumstances (who, where, when) steer every idea. Assessed by an idea sheet and a short spoken or written reason, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: job; revise; review; audience; small group; show
notes: Name the jobs a showing needs, revise by repeating and reviewing together, and show the small group's work to classmates as the audience. What changes: named jobs and a repeat-and-review cycle with a critique. Assessed by a rehearsed showing and a critique-and-revise note, scored on a short rubric for preparation, role and revision. Teacher note: the unit's one critique follows describe, ask, suggest, and ties feedback to a look-for. A child who does not want to perform takes a job or records a take.

words: technique; exercise; practice; choose; posture; character
cross_subject: ela:SL.4.4 (tell a story in order, speaking clearly)
notes: Choose how your body moves to build a character, practice chosen exercises for group work, and build body and voice techniques you can name. What changes: the child chooses the exercise and practices it as a technique. Assessed by a short performance and a self-check, scored on a short rubric for voice, body and a clear character.

words: lighting; sound; set; snag; central idea; given circumstances
notes: Plan sets, lights and sound that serve a story's given circumstances, suggest ways to use tech in a play, and fix snags that appear in rehearsal as a group. What changes: lights and sound serve a central idea and snags are fixed as a group. Assessed by a design sketch or model with a written reason, scored on a short rubric for fit to the story and care in making. Teacher note: bright or flashing lights are never used, and sharp tools come only after a safe-handling check.

words: rewrite; outcome; culture; era; practice; storytelling
notes: Rewrite dialogue and actions so a story ends differently, look at how storytelling differs across cultures, and compare the stage practices of one past era with today's. What changes: the child rewrites an outcome and compares eras and cultures. Assessed by a short written or staged response about one story, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: perspective; local; problem; compare; costume; culture
notes: Name ways drama work reflects a community's or culture's perspectives, react to local and social problems with other subjects worked into drama, and compare characters' qualities through looks, props and costumes that show cultural views. What changes: drama is used to react to a local problem. Assessed by a short written or spoken response naming one community tie and one other-subject tie, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: choice; compare; contrast; feeling; body; spot
notes: Pick out the choices artists made in a piece while joining in and watching, compare your experiences, and talk about how feelings change the body. What changes: experiences are compared and feelings are read in the body. Assessed by an audience-journal entry citing one choice an artist made, scored on a three-line guide.

words: offer; judge; choice; audience; character; way
notes: Offer a way of judging a drama piece, and notice how a character's choice changes what an audience sees. What changes: the child offers a way of judging. Assessed by a short response to a showing with a reason, scored on a three-line guide.

words: inner; quality; thought; situation; original; question
notes: Name physical qualities that could show what a character is like inside, picture how inner thoughts shape the story, and shape original ideas from group questions about characters and the situations they face. What changes: ideas come from a character's inner life, not only the plot. Assessed by an idea sheet and a short spoken or written reason, scored on a three-line rubric.

words: job; self-review; revise; viewer; share; relaxed
notes: Take on a set job in a piece, revise by repeating and reviewing your own work, and share the piece in a relaxed way with viewers. What changes: each child owns a job and reviews their own work alone. Assessed by a rehearsed showing and a critique-and-revise note, scored on a short rubric for preparation, role and revision.

words: physical; meaning; exercise; fit; build; character
notes: Let physical choices carry meaning, pick acting exercises that fit a piece, and use body and voice to build a character. What changes: exercises are matched to the piece and the body carries meaning. Assessed by a short performance and a self-check, scored on a short rubric for voice, body and a clear character.

words: theme; design; tech; express; problem; fix
notes: Suggest design ideas for a play's given circumstances, show how tech elements are used, invent fixes for rehearsal problems, and judge how tech expresses a theme. What changes: tech elements express a theme and the child invents the fixes. Assessed by a design sketch or model with a written reason, scored on a short rubric for fit to the story and care in making.

words: motive; hidden; compare; source; custom; term
cross_subject: ela:RL.5.3 (compare characters and events)
notes: Describe the hidden thoughts and feelings behind what characters say and do, compare stories from different cultures before making a play, and find old sources on the terms and customs of the theatre. What changes: motives are named and stories from several cultures are compared before a play is made. Assessed by a short written or staged response about one story, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: link; community; worldwide; past; view; response
notes: Explain how drama joins a person to a community and its culture, look at past, worldwide and social problems that drama voices, and say how cultural views shape your response to characters. What changes: past and worldwide problems join local ones. Assessed by a short written or spoken response naming one community tie and one other-subject tie, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: react; defend; stance; breath; pitch; experience
notes: Explain how you reacted to artists' decisions, defend your reactions from your own experience, and trace how feelings show in stance, movement, breath and pitch. What changes: responses are defended and feelings are traced to breath, stance and pitch. Assessed by an audience-journal entry citing one choice an artist made, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: breath and stance work is gentle and optional.

words: create; guide; situation; audience; view; judge
notes: Make a way of judging drama work and use it, and notice how a character's situation changes what an audience thinks of a piece. What changes: the child creates a judging guide and uses it. Assessed by a short response to a showing with a reason, scored on a three-line guide.

words: staging; problem; fix; analyze; decision; devise
notes: Find possible fixes for staging problems in a drama work, and sharpen your ideas and artistic decisions by analyzing them in devised or scripted work. words: pattern; AB; ABA; form; tool; phrase
notes: Try choreographic tools to make simple patterns and forms such as AB and ABA, and make a phrase that shows a feeling or concept and discuss how the choices affected it. What changes: named forms and tools replace free improvising. Assessed by a performed AB or ABA phrase and a short discussion, scored on a short rubric.

words: alter; tool; option; form; study; main idea
notes: Alter choreographic tools to widen the options for patterns and forms, and build a dance study around a main idea while discussing how well the choices worked. What changes: tools are changed on purpose and the study has a main idea. Assessed by a performed study and a short written or spoken evaluation, scored on a short rubric.

words: expand; communicate; without words; chosen moves; tools; study
notes: Alter several choreographic tools together to open up options and sharpen the main idea, and build a study from chosen moves while talking about how dance says things without words. What changes: several tools are changed together and the student reflects on how the study means something, where grade 4 altered tools for one study. Assessed by a performed study and a short reflection scored on a short rubric.

words: purposeful; goal; criteria; personal; cultural; judge
notes: Build a dance study toward a goal you set, using choreographic tools and forms, and write criteria for a personal or cultural study to judge which moves say it best. What changes: the study has a stated goal and the student's own criteria, where grade 5 built a study around a main idea. Assessed by a performed study plus a criteria sheet scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: shape; vary; criteria; meaning; explain; study
notes: Shape a study with varied tools and forms and explain the choices, and define criteria for a personal or cultural study and explain how they carry its meaning. What changes: criteria are defined and explained, where grade 6 wrote and applied them. Assessed by a performed study and a written explanation scored on a short rubric.

words: together; new dance; group; process; apply; effect
notes: Choose tools and forms together for a new dance, describe how the group worked, and define and apply criteria for a personal or cultural dance. What changes: the work is made with others and the group process is described, where grade 7 made a study alone. Assessed by a group performance and a process description, scored on a short rubric.

words: collaborate; structure; purpose; artist's statement; support; elements
notes: Make a dance with others whose structure serves its purpose, and write an artist's statement on how structure and elements support it. What changes: a written artist's statement joins the making, where grade 8 only defined criteria. Assessed by a performed dance and its written statement, scored on a short rubric for structure, purpose and reasons.

words: original; design; composition; aesthetic; statement; analyze
notes: Design original dances alone and with others, analyze how their structure and composition serve the purpose, and write a statement of your aesthetic that guides your choices. What changes: a personal aesthetic is stated and composition is analyzed, where level 1 wrote about one dance's purpose. Assessed by a portfolio entry of a dance with an aesthetic statement, scored on a short rubric.

words: fluency; personal voice; heighten; viewpoint; cultural; justify
notes: Choreograph original dances with fluency and a personal voice, justify choices that heighten the purpose, and write a statement of your own cultural and artistic viewpoint. What changes: fluent original work and a viewpoint stated. Assessed by a portfolio of original dances and a defended statement, scored on the Level 3 rubric. Teacher note: a student names only a heritage they choose to name; no one is asked to represent a group.

words: change; guide; improvise; draw; move; symbol
notes: Change movements when given suggestions in guided improvisation, and sketch or symbolize a dance move. What changes: first year, try a change and draw a move. Assessed by a teacher observation of one changed move and a drawn symbol, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: suggestion; remember; sequence; picture; symbol; jump
notes: Try suggested changes to movements in improvisation and in a short remembered sequence, and draw pictures or symbols for kinds of moves such as jump, turn and slide. What changes: a remembered sequence is changed and moves get symbols. Assessed by a changed sequence and a page of move symbols, marked met, partly or not yet.

words: choice; high; middle; low; level; recalled
notes: Make choices and try suggestions that change movement in improvisation or a remembered sequence, and draw symbols for high, middle and low levels. What changes: the child draws levels as symbols and chooses a change, where grade 1 drew move types. Assessed by a showing of a changed sequence and a level drawing, scored on a three-line guide.

words: feedback; alter; describe; route; map; direction
notes: Use feedback to change the movements in a brief piece and describe what changed, and chart your phrase's directions and routes with a sketch map or symbols. What changes: feedback drives a revision and a pathway map is made. Assessed by a revised phrase, a one-line description of the change and a route map, scored on a short rubric.

words: classmates; comment; reflection; intent; relate; beside
notes: Rework movement using classmates' comments and your own reflection to sharpen the intent, and sketch how dancers stand in relation to each other, such as beside, above or behind. What changes: comments and the dancer's own reflection both drive the rework, and relationships between dancers are drawn. Assessed by a revised piece, an explanation of choices and a relationship sketch, scored on a short rubric.

words: peer; suggestion; widen; refine; log; video
notes: Try peer suggestions to widen the options for a brief piece and explain the refinements, and log what changed in your sequence with words, drawings or a recording. What changes: a change log is kept as the work grows. Assessed by a revised piece and its change log scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: no student is recorded, photographed or filmed without the family's yes; a face or voice is never required (hands, the work or the sound alone will do); a student who does not want to be recorded is observed live and the teacher's mark stands; kept work stays on the student's, family's or school's own device.

words: criteria; group; revise; fit; own method; write down
notes: Revise a dance against criteria your group built and explain how each revision fits the intent, and invent your own way of writing down a sequence of moves. What changes: the group builds the criteria and the student invents a way to record moves, where grade 5 logged changes. Assessed by a revised dance and a written sequence in the student's own method, scored on a short rubric.

words: judge; adjust; standards; notation; established; record
notes: Judge possible revisions, even adjusting your own standards, and explain how they clarify the intent, and study an established notation method for recording a sequence in writing, signs or a recording. What changes: revisions are judged against shifting standards and a real notation method is studied. Assessed by a revised dance and a notated sequence, scored on a short rubric.

words: alone; collaborative; excerpt; strengthen; part; notation
notes: Revise choreography alone or with others using criteria and feedback and explain how the revisions strengthen the intent, and try parts of an established notation method to record a dance excerpt. What changes: the revision is independent or shared and an excerpt is notated. Assessed by a revised piece and a notated excerpt, scored on a short rubric.

words: devices; structure; evaluate; compare; notation; section
notes: Clarify a dance's purpose by reworking its devices and structure and judge how the revisions affected it, and compare established notation methods for recording a section. What changes: devices and structure are reworked, and notation methods are compared, where grade 8 tried one method on an excerpt. Assessed by a revised dance with an evaluation and a notated section, scored on a short rubric.

words: refine; criteria; feedback; strategy; media; plan
notes: Refine devices and structure using criteria and feedback and judge your own revisions, and plan how to record a whole dance with notation or media. What changes: a recording plan covers a whole dance, where level 1 notated a section. Assessed by a refined dance and a recording plan, scored on a short rubric.

words: document; justify; reflection; complete; notation; record
notes: Refine devices, structures and criteria through reflection and feedback, document and defend each revision, and record a complete dance with an established notation method. What changes: a whole dance is notated and every revision is defended, where level 2 only planned the recording. Assessed by a portfolio entry of the revision record and the notated dance, scored on the Level 3 rubric.

words: shape; line; level; size; tempo; quick
notes: Show shapes with lines, levels and sizes in a group circle, match your speed to the tempo of sounds, and move with different qualities such as quick, floppy or sharp. What changes: space, time and energy meet as three simple ideas, with no dance elements named before. Assessed by a short movement task marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: this unit names the elements and does not drill the motor skill, which physical education teaches.

words: path; zigzag; curved; beat; slow; bouncy
notes: Change shape, level and facing, travel on curved and zigzag paths in lines and circles, move at three speeds to a steady beat, and name qualities such as bouncy or floppy. What changes: paths, speeds and quality words are named, where kindergarten only showed shapes and sizes. Assessed by a movement task with a spoken quality word, scored on a three-line guide.

words: direction; symmetrical; phrase; strong beat; circle; turn
notes: Move with clear direction, find symmetrical and uneven shapes, tell short phrases from long ones, land on strong beats in two- or three-beat music, and pick words for qualities and dance them. What changes: phrase length and strong beats are heard and shown, where grade 1 kept a steady beat. Assessed by a movement task and a quality word, scored on a three-line guide.

words: space; dimension; focus; phrasing; dynamics; energy
notes: Judge distance and work in all dimensions with focus, improvise to fill a set time while keeping the music's timing, and vary energy to give movements specific qualities. What changes: the dancer judges distance and timing alone, where grade 2 followed set directions. Assessed by a short improvised performance scored on a short rubric for space, time and energy.

words: fixed; changing; rhythm; percussion; tempo shift; analyze
notes: Make fixed and changing shapes and connect with eye contact, play percussion for dancers, move to steady and irregular rhythms, and describe changes in energy in vivid words. Land jumps softly. What changes: irregular rhythms are answered and energy is described in words, where grade 3 stayed with the music's timing. Assessed by a performed phrase and a spoken analysis, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: ground; aerial; project; contrast; tight; flowing
notes: Combine shapes with ground and aerial paths, dance to rhythms made inside and outside the body, and contrast tight and flowing movement started from the torso or from the limbs. What changes: contrast is added to projection, where grade 4 described energy changes. Assessed by a performed phrase scored on a short rubric for space, timing and contrast. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: partner; group; abrupt; lingering; measure; tension
notes: Refine partner and group skills by judging distance and varying paths, mix abrupt and lingering timing with the right beats in three- and four-beat measures, and use muscle tension to start movement and show dynamics. What changes: partner and group spacing and measures of three and four. Assessed by a group performance scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: borrow; style; accent; variation; compare; plan
notes: Broaden your ground and aerial patterns by borrowing body designs from other styles, vary timing with accents, and compare movement qualities across styles and plan how to perform them clearly. What changes: styles are compared on their elements, where grade 6 refined partner spacing. Assessed by a performed phrase and a short comparison, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: a style is borrowed only from a community's own published teaching or a named practitioner. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it. no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: sculpt; props; surroundings; breath; separate tempo; texture
notes: Sculpt shapes around other dancers, props and the room while keeping eye focus, choose beat, movement and breath phrasing with separate tempos for body parts, and texture movement by steering energy. What changes: patterns are complex and timing is layered, where grade 7 varied accents. Assessed by a performed phrase scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: partner; balance; contrast; syncopation; accent; whole body
notes: Build partner and group skills with balances at contrasting levels, use syncopation and accents at varied tempos, take cues from accompaniment, and use energy through the whole body. What changes: partner balances and syncopation arrive, with a solo version of every balance always offered. Assessed by a performed phrase scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; balances are low to the floor, by agreement, with a solo version always offered.

words: complex; purposeful; unpredictable; inner rhythm; initiate; transition
notes: Dance alone or with others using space on purpose in ground and aerial sequences, use unpredictable timing with phrasing from an inner rhythm, and start each phrase with energy that flows into the next. What changes: space is used on purpose and timing is unpredictable, where level 1 built balances and syncopation. Assessed by a performed sequence scored on the Level 2 rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: fullest range; audience; layered; phrasing; project; dynamics
notes: Use the fullest range of space with focus moving inward and outward toward an audience, layer several rhythms with or without music, and adjust dynamics over a broad range to carry an intent. What changes: the full spatial range is used toward an audience and rhythms are layered, where level 2 used space and timing on purpose. Assessed by a performed sequence scored on the Level 3 rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered.

words: copy; pattern; safe; space; start; stop
cross_subject: physical-education:k-in-place (in-place movement in a personal space)
notes: Copy matching-side and crossing moves, shapes and body patterns, move safely in shared space and start and stop on a cue, and relate body parts to each other and repeat movements on request. What changes: first year, safe shared space and copying. Assessed by a teacher observation of the cue and a repeated move, marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: personal space and stopping on the cue come first. The motor skill itself is taught in physical education.

words: pattern; travel; formation; group; change; own space
cross_subject: physical-education:g1-dance-moves (the traveling and in-place moves)
notes: Show many ways to travel and stay still with different shapes and directions, move safely in group formations while keeping your own space, and change moves or layouts when asked. What changes: formations and asked changes are added, where kindergarten copied moves and stopped on a cue. Assessed by a teacher observation of a group task, marked met, partly or not yet. The motor moves come from physical education.

words: pathway; spatial; share; repeat; aware; adjust
cross_subject: physical-education:g2-dance-sequence (a short linked move sequence)
notes: Perform travelling and in-place moves and body patterns along varied pathways, move safely in different group formations, and repeat movements while staying aware of others. What changes: awareness of others while repeating moves, where grade 1 changed formations when asked. Assessed by a repeated sequence in a group, scored on a three-line guide. The motor sequence is taught in physical education.

words: align; strong; copy; recall; partner; coach
cross_subject: physical-education:g3-dance-steps (dance steps in short phrases)
notes: Copy shapes, qualities and patterns in a sequence while keeping the body aligned and strong, coordinate with partners to change levels, directions and paths safely, and recall sequences in pairs or groups using coaching and your own checks. What changes: recall in pairs and groups with a self-check. Assessed by a recalled sequence scored on a short rubric. The motor steps come from physical education.

words: balance; alignment; strengthen; injury; cue; synchronize
cross_subject: physical-education:g4-dance-sequence (linked moves in a dance sequence)
notes: Use alignment and balance when copying and recalling patterns, do strengthening exercises and explain how technique, avoiding injury and food choices connect, and match phrases with other dancers using music or lighting cues. What changes: syncing with others and linking technique to health. Assessed by a performed phrase and a short explanation, scored on a short rubric. The motor sequence is taught in physical education. Health habits lean on the health course, not here. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: run of phrases; clarity; habits; nutrition; ensemble; goals
cross_subject: physical-education:g5-gym-dance-sequence (a longer routine of dance parts)
notes: Recall and perform a run of phrases with alignment and clarity, practice safe body habits and say how they and nutrition prevent injury, and rehearse with an ensemble to match timing and set goals from feedback. What changes: a longer run of phrases is rehearsed with set goals, where grade 4 matched single phrases to cues. Assessed by an ensemble performance and a goals note, scored on a short rubric. Physical education teaches the motor routine. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: direction change; jump; landing; transition; anatomy; warm up
cross_subject: physical-education:g6-dance-sequences (eight-count phrases and transitions)
notes: Carry out direction changes, jumps, landings and transitions cleanly, warm up safely using anatomy and body signals, and improve an ensemble dance by spotting what works and testing fixes. What changes: transitions are clean and the warm-up is understood, where grade 5 set rehearsal goals. Assessed by a performed ensemble dance and a growth note scored on a short rubric. Physical education teaches the motor phrases. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: adapt; growing; weight shift; healthy; peers; group goals
cross_subject: physical-education:g7-dance-ideas (movement ideas in dance forms)
notes: Adapt body use to a growing body while applying alignment and weight shifts, practice healthy habits and discuss the benefits, and rehearse dances with peers and set group goals after watching professional dancers. What changes: technique is adapted to the changing body. Assessed by a rehearsed ensemble piece and a goals note, scored on a short rubric. Physical education teaches the dance ideas. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: embody; spatial design; rhythmic phrase; evaluate; accuracy; record
cross_subject: physical-education:g8-fitness-dance-apply (dance routines done with correct form); health:g8-phw-habits-personal-community (healthy habits in dance and daily life)
notes: Copy, recall and perform spatial designs and rhythmic phrases, rate health habits in dance and daily life, using an invented dancer for food and body, and plan ways to improve, and work with peers on accuracy while tracking your own progress. What changes: personal goals and a progress record are kept, where grade 7 set group goals. Assessed by a performed piece and a progress record scored on a short rubric. Physical education teaches the routine form. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: retain; choreography; plan; habits; rehearsal; video
cross_subject: physical-education:g9-dance-design (learning and designing dance sequences); health:g9-phw-evaluate-habits (judging habits that prevent injury)
notes: Retain and perform choreography with technical skill, plan healthy habits for dance and daily life, with food through an invented dancer, and plan rehearsals with peers, using a recording to analyze and justify practice choices. What changes: rehearsals are planned and analyzed from a recording, where grade 8 kept a personal progress record. Assessed by a rehearsal plan, a performed piece and an analysis, scored on a short rubric. Physical education designs and performs sequences too. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. No student is recorded, photographed or filmed without the family's yes; a face or voice is never required (hands, the work or the sound alone will do); a student who does not want to be recorded is observed live and the teacher's mark stands; kept work stays on the student's, family's or school's own device. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: demanding; goals; anatomy; eating plan; solo; reflect
notes: Dance demanding sequences of space, rhythm and dynamics with others to meet goals, apply anatomy and healthy habits to technique, with an invented dancer's eating plan, and plan solo and group rehearsals and reflect on them. What changes: demanding sequences are met and solo and group rehearsals are planned, where level 1 planned one rehearsal. Assessed by a performed sequence and a rehearsal reflection, scored on the Level 2 rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: body-mind; complex; self-evaluate; research; lead; rehearsal
notes: Use body-mind principles in complex solo, partner or ensemble work and judge yourself, research safe dancer practices and change your own, and lead rehearsals that attend to detail and expression. What changes: rehearsals are led by the student and safe practice is researched, where level 2 planned rehearsals. Assessed by a led rehearsal, a performed piece and a research note, scored on the Level 3 rubric. Teacher note: no lifts; partner contact only by agreement and never required; a solo version is always offered. Teacher note: no task asks about a student's own diet, weight or body; food choices and eating plans are studied through an invented dancer or dancers in general (APPROACH.md, "Sensitive ground").

words: perform; space; audience; prop; choose; together
notes: Dance in a marked area for others and alongside them, and choose one prop to use in a dance. What changes: first year, a marked space and one prop. Assessed by a short showing marked met, partly or not yet on a three-line guide. Teacher note: a child may dance in a pair or watch first; no stage lights or hot materials.

words: audience; seated; apart; prop; improve; show
notes: Dance for an audience seated apart from the dancers, and try simple props to see if they improve a performance. What changes: the audience is seated apart, where kindergarten danced beside others in a marked area. Assessed by a short showing to a seated class, scored on a three-line guide.

words: zone; viewer; backdrop; projected; extra; staging
notes: Perform where viewers and dancers sit in separate zones, and try a few extras such as a small prop, a backdrop or a projected image. What changes: separate zones and staging extras are added, where grade 1 used simple props. Assessed by a short showing in a marked zone, scored on a three-line guide.

words: left; right; center; costume; scenery; lighting
notes: Learn the stage areas by name (left, right, center), and try simple costumes, music, scenery or lighting in a dance made for a set space. What changes: stage words and a first design choice, where grade 2 used extras without naming areas. Assessed by a performed dance and a labelled stage sketch, scored on a short rubric.

words: formal stage; gym; plan; production; purpose; experience
notes: Plan how to turn a gym or a lawn into a formal-feeling stage, and try production elements to strengthen the dance's purpose and the audience's experience. What changes: a plain room is planned as a stage, where grade 3 named stage areas and tried design choices. Assessed by a stage plan and a performed dance, scored on a short rubric.

words: venue; adapt; spacing; staging; features; suit
notes: Adapt one dance to different venues by changing spacing and moves, and choose staging features that strengthen its purpose and suit several venues. What changes: one dance is adapted for more than one venue, where grade 4 planned one stage. Assessed by a performed dance in two spaces and a staging note, scored on a short rubric.

words: manners; notes; choreographer; production terms; compare; choose
notes: Adapt moves to the space, practice performance manners, apply the choreographer's notes, and compare production elements and explain your choices with production terms. What changes: etiquette and notes are applied and choices are explained in production terms, where grade 5 adapted one dance to venues. Assessed by a performed dance and an explanation, scored on a short rubric.

words: recommend; etiquette; journal; venue; audience; explain
notes: Recommend how to adapt a space, follow etiquette, keep a rehearsal journal and apply the choreographer's notes, and explain how production elements would change for another venue or audience. What changes: a rehearsal journal and recommendations for other venues, where grade 6 explained choices once. Assessed by a performed dance and its journal, scored on a short rubric.

words: lead; prepare; document; improve; carry out; design
notes: Lead preparation, follow etiquette, record your efforts, plan improvements and apply notes, and design and carry out staging features together for varied venues. What changes: students lead and design, where grade 7 recommended and journaled. Assessed by a led showing, a preparation record and a staging design, scored on a short rubric.

words: leadership; documented; evaluate; production design; strengthen; options
notes: Lead with etiquette, apply notes, evaluate documented rehearsal methods with proper terms, and judge production design options and carry out the ones that serve the dance's purpose. What changes: rehearsal methods and design options are evaluated, where grade 8 led and designed. Assessed by a performed dance, a rehearsal evaluation and a design choice, scored on a short rubric.

words: model; projection; concert; stage; plan; process
notes: Model leadership and etiquette, strengthen projection, apply notes, judge your documented process, and work together to stage a concert in a theater or other space with a production plan. What changes: a whole concert is staged, where level 1 evaluated one dance's production. Assessed by the concert and a production plan, scored on the Level 2 rubric. Teacher note: a concert uses only dances that are original to the class, public domain or openly licensed.

words: lead; portfolio; venues; organize; design; document
notes: Lead, model etiquette, build projection strategies, compile a portfolio of your process, and stage concerts in several venues, designing the production for each. What changes: more than one venue and a process portfolio, where level 2 staged one concert. Assessed by the concerts and a portfolio, scored on the Level 3 rubric.

words: notice; repeat; describe; stand out; why; dance words
notes: Spot a move that comes back in a dance, show or tell about moves you watched or did, describe movements with easy dance words, and show one movement that stood out and say why. What changes: first year, one repeated move and one favorite. Assessed by a spoken or shown answer marked met, partly or not yet. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: pattern; style; culture; idea; stand for; interesting
notes: Spot a repeating move that forms a pattern, show and describe movements from a style or culture, pick movements that stand for an idea, and say why you chose eye-catching moves. What changes: patterns and ideas are tied to movement, where kindergarten noticed one repeated move. Assessed by a short showing and a sentence that uses a dance word and points to a move, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: build; pattern; clue; meaning; tradition; works well
notes: Spot moves that build into a pattern, show and describe moves from dances of different styles or cultures, use movement clues to find a dance's meaning, and say what makes a watched dance work well. What changes: the student points to a clue in the dance to claim a meaning, where grade 1 tied ideas to moves. Assessed by a written or spoken sentence with a clue from the dance, scored on a three-line guide. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: phrase; pattern; differ; context clue; central idea; similar
cross_subject: ela:SL.3.1 (class talk about a dance that was watched)
notes: Spot how a pattern of moves builds a phrase, show how two styles or traditions differ, pick context clues in movement and tie them to the central idea, and describe likenesses and differences between styles. What changes: two styles are compared side by side, where grade 2 used clues from one dance. Assessed by a short written response with a reason and a clue, scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: theme; style; genre; setting; decode; artistic
notes: Spot movement patterns across dances that shape a theme or style, show how styles differ within one genre, use movement, ideas and setting together to read a dance's meaning, and say what makes a dance artistic. What changes: the setting joins the clues in reading a meaning, where grade 3 compared two styles. Assessed by a written response scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: the unseen dance is a written description or a live demonstration by the teacher. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: meaning; purpose; culture; compare; interpret; traits
cross_subject: ela:W.5.1 (an opinion supported by reasons)
notes: Find a dance's meaning from its movement patterns, describe your own culture's dance style in basic terms if you choose to share it and compare it with another, and say what makes a dance artistic in terms of its elements. What changes: interpretation names the traits that carry the idea, where grade 4 used movement, ideas and setting as clues. Assessed by a written response with evidence scored on a short rubric. Teacher note: a student describes only a style they choose to share. A sacred or ceremonial work is used only when its source says it is open to be taught, and never as an exercise, warm-up, costume or imitation; any cultural claim is checked against a source before a unit names it.

words: relate; terms; elements; technique; criteria; critique
cross_subject: ela:SL.6.1 (discussion with evidence)
notes: Describe how repeating patterns relate in a dance, explain how dance elements work across styles with specific terms, explain how technique, structure and context carry purpose, and build your own criteria to critique a dance. What changes: the student builds the criteria, where grade 5 defined what makes a dance artistic. Assessed by a written critique using their criteria, scored on a short rubric.
